1.note: The author is speaking as if **days** were objects and as if Job were a container that was **full** of them. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And David was old, having lived for many days]

The expressions **old** and **full of days** mean similar things. The author is using them together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Your language may have a characteristic expression that it would use in such a context. Alternate translation: [And David was very old] or [And David had lived to be an old man]

3.note: The expression **were counted** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [And he had the leaders count the Levites]

In certain contexts, biblical authors and characters use the expression **son of** to indicate that a person has the characteristic of something. In this case, the author is saying that these Levites had the characteristic of being at least **30 years** old. Alternate translation: [who were at least 30 years old]

3.q: וַ⁠יְהִ֨י מִסְפָּרָ֤⁠ם לְ⁠גֻלְגְּלֹתָ⁠ם֙ לִ⁠גְבָרִ֔ים שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וּ⁠שְׁמוֹנָ֖ה אָֽלֶף
3.note: The author is using **by their skulls** as a common expression of his culture to mean “individually.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and the headcount of the males was 38,000] or [and the counting was of individuals, specifically of males, 38,000]

The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and the total was 38,000]

4.note: This verse and the next verse present a direct quotation from David. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language. Alternate translation: [And David commanded, “From these]

4.q: לְ⁠נַצֵּ֨חַ֙ עַל־מְלֶ֣אכֶת בֵּית־יְהוָ֔ה עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְ⁠אַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָ֑לֶף וְ⁠שֹׁטְרִ֥ים וְ⁠שֹׁפְטִ֖ים שֵׁ֥שֶׁת אֲלָפִֽים
4.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about how many Levites would have each role before the information about the roles themselves. Alternate translation: [I want 24,000 to lead over the work of the house of Yahweh, 6,000 to be officers and judges]

David seems to mean that these 24,000 Levites would supervise the people who worked in the temple area as servants to them and to the priests, whom the author mentions in 9:2. However, these Levites also did work in the temple area themselves. You may be able to use an expression in your translation that indicates both of these things. The UST models one way to do that.

David is speaking of the temple that the Israelites will build for Yahweh as if it were going to be a **house** in which Yahweh would live. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly, here and in the rest of the chapter. Alternate translation: [the temple of Yahweh]

4.q: לְ⁠נַצֵּ֨חַ֙ עַל־מְלֶ֣אכֶת בֵּית־יְהוָ֔ה עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְ⁠אַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָ֑לֶף וְ⁠שֹׁטְרִ֥ים וְ⁠שֹׁפְטִ֖ים שֵׁ֥שֶׁת אֲלָפִֽים
4.note: If you decided in the previous verse to put the information about how many Levites would have each role before the information about the roles themselves, you can word this verse in such a way as to complete the sentence you began there. Alternate translation: [4,000 to be gatekeepers, and 4,000 to be praisers of Yahweh with the instruments that I made for praising]

7.note: The author is not referring to a specific **Gershonite**. He means the Gershonites in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [The two main divisions of the Gershonites were the descendants of Ladan and the descendants of Shimei]

8.note: The author is speaking as if the family of **Ladan** had been a body and **Jehiel** had been its **head**. He means that Jehiel was the leader of his generation. The implication is that he was the firstborn son. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly, here and in the rest of this chapter. Alternate translation: [the leader] or [the firstborn]

11.note: The name **Zizah** appears here in the standard Hebrew text as we have it today. It is a variant of the name “Zina” in the previous verse, which appears here in the ancient Greek translation, suggesting that it may have been the original reading. You may want to use the name “Zina” here, particularly if there is a major translation in your area and it uses that name. Alternate translation: [Zina]

13.note: The expression **was separated** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [And Yahweh separated Aaron]

Here, **holy of holies** means extremely or uniquely holy. If this possessive form would not express in your language that Aaron and his descendants became holy in a way that the other Levites did not, you can express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [to be holy in a unique way] or [to be holy in a way that the other Levites were not]
Here and in the next verse, the term **sons** means “descendants.” Alternate translation: [and his descendants]

Here, the **face** of **Yahweh** represents his “presence.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in Yahweh’s presence]

The author is using one aspect of Yahweh, his **name**, to mean all of him in the act of being blessed by the priests. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and to bless him]
Here, Yahweh’s **name** represents his authority. Alternate translation: [by his authority]

14.note: The author is using the possessive form to describe a **man** who was characterized by having a special role to represent **God** to the Israelites. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [God’s special representative]

The author is using **were called after** as a common expression of his culture to mean “were considered to belong to.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [his descendants were considered to belong to the tribe of Levi]

The author means specifically that the descendants of Moses were considered Levites rather than priests. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [his descendants were considered to be Levites]

The expression **were called** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [his descendants were Levites, not priests]

17.note: See how you translated the expression “to above” in 22:5. Alternate translation: [were very many]

22.note: The **sons of Kish** were not the literal **brothers** of the **daughters** of Eleazar. Your language may have a kinship term that you can use to make this clear in your translation. Alternate translation: [their cousins]

The author is using **lifted** as a common expression of his culture to mean “married.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [married them]

24.note: In this verse, the author is offering a summary to conclude the list of Levite clans. Use a natural way in your language to offer a summary that concludes a section.

The author is not referring to a specific **house** or **doer**. He means those things in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [according to the houses of … the doers of]

In this context, the expression **the house of their fathers** describes the clans of the Levites, and the expression **heads of fathers** describes the ancestors of those clans. Alternate translation: [according to their clans, based on who their ancestors were]

Here, the **names** of the Levites represent the men who had those names. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in the counting of men]
See how you translated the same expression in 23:3. Alternate translation: [individually]
To translate this expression here and in verse 27, see how you translated the similar expression in 23:3. Alternate translation: [who were at least 30 years old]

While the author says in verse 3 that the Israelites counted the Levites who were at least 30 years old, and he says here that they counted those who were at least 20 years old, the author explains the reason for the difference in the next three verses. So you do not need to account for that difference here, either in the text of your translation or in a footnote.

25.note: The author is using the term **For** to introduce the reason why the Israelites counted Levites who were at least 20 years old, after originally planning to count those who were at least 30 years old. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [They counted Levites who were at least 20 years old because]

27.note: The author is using the term **words** to represent what David commanded by using words. He would mean not that these were the very **last** commands that David gave but that they were commands he gave near the end of his life and reign. Alternate translation: [in obedience to what David commanded near the end of his life]
Here, **sons** means “descendants.” Alternate translation: [the descendants of Levi] or [the Levites]

28.note: Some interpreters believe that verses 28–32 are a continuation of the quotation of David in verses 25–26, with verse 27 being an explanatory aside from the author. Some versions of the Bible reflect this interpretation. See the discussion in the introduction to this chapter of how you might present verses 25–32 if you decide to follow this interpretation in your translation.

If verses 28–32 are not a continuation of the quotation of David, then the word **For** would introduce the reason why so many Levites were needed that the count was expanded to include those who were at least 20 years old. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [The reason why so many Levites were needed was that]

Here, **at the hand of** represents “next to.” The idea is that the Levites worked alongside the priests as their assistants. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [they worked next to the sons of Aaron] or [they served as assistants to the sons of Aaron]

The author is describing the priests by reference to the way they were **sons** or descendants of Aaron. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers, here and in verse 32. Alternate translation: [the priests]

The author is speaking as if the Levites were actually **over** or on top of these things. He means that they were responsible for them If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [with responsibility for the courts and the chambers and the purifying of]

The author is using the adjective **holy** as a noun to mean a certain kind of thing. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase, here and in verse 32. Alternate translation: [all of the holy implements]

Since the author has already specified at the start of the verse that the Levites were responsible for this, here he appears to mean that the Levites were responsible for any other necessary aspects of this work that he has not listed. Alternate translation: [and for anything else that was required for the work of the service of the God’s temple]

29.note: The author is using a representative **pan** in which the Levites would have baked the **bread of the arrangement** and the **wafers of unleavened bread** to mean the act of baking itself. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and for baking them]

30.q: בַּ⁠בֹּ֣קֶר בַּ⁠בֹּ֔קֶר לְ⁠הֹד֥וֹת וּ⁠לְ⁠הַלֵּ֖ל לַ⁠יהוָ֑ה וְ⁠כֵ֖ן לָ⁠עָֽרֶב
30.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information that the Levites sang to Yahweh in the **evening** with the information that they did so in the **morning**. Alternate translation: [by morning, by morning, and thus in the evening, to thank and to praise Yahweh] or [every morning and every evening to thank and to praise Yahweh]

The author is using **by morning, by morning** as a common expression of his culture to mean “every morning.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [morning after morning] or [every morning]

31.q: וּ⁠לְ⁠כֹ֨ל הַעֲל֤וֹת עֹלוֹת֙ לַ⁠יהוָ֔ה לַ⁠שַּׁבָּת֔וֹת לֶ⁠חֳדָשִׁ֖ים וְ⁠לַ⁠מֹּעֲדִ֑ים בְּ⁠מִסְפָּ֨ר
31.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information that the Levites were responsible for preparing the right **number** of animals with the information that these were for **burnt offerings**. Alternate translation: [and for every offering of burnt offerings by number to Yahweh on the Sabbaths, at the new moons, and at the annual festivals] or [and for the right number of burnt offerings for every offering to Yahweh on the Sabbaths, at the new moons, and at the annual festivals]

Here, Yahweh’s **face** represents his presence. Since Yahweh was considered to be especially present at his temple, this could be a reference to the temple area. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in Yahweh’s presence] or [at Yahweh’s temple]

32.q: וְ⁠שָׁמְר֞וּ אֶת־מִשְׁמֶ֣רֶת אֹֽהֶל־מוֹעֵ֗ד וְ⁠אֵת֙ מִשְׁמֶ֣רֶת הַ⁠קֹּ֔דֶשׁ וּ⁠מִשְׁמֶ֕רֶת בְּנֵ֥י אַהֲרֹ֖ן
32.note: The author is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [And they cared for the tent of meeting and for the holy and for the sons of Aaron]

The author is speaking of the priests as if they were actual **brothers** of the Levites. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [their kinsmen]
